articleTitle: Frequency Limited Model Reference Adaptive Control for Unmanned Underwater Vehicle
abstract: Controlling of unmanned underwater vehicles (UUV) is a complicated challenge due to the nonlinear dynamics, uncertainty in model parameters, and external disturbances that exist in underwater environments. Therefore, compared to classical control techniques, adaptive control is a promising solution to address these issues. However, to realize its complete potential in underwater vehicle applications, the trade-offs among rapid transient performance and smooth control signals must be carefully analysed. When using high learning rates to improve the transient performance of systems controlled using Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC), it has been observed that it results in undesirable high frequency oscillations in control signals. Frequency Limited Model Reference Adaptive Control (FLMRAC) is a technique that adds a mismatch term to the reference system of MRAC. Addition of this term provides better control compared to standard MRAC by filtering out high-frequency content of the tracking error. This results in filtering of high-frequency content from the control signal, which in turn helps to avoid high frequency oscillations. Simulation results also show that FLMRAC results in a lower tracking error as well as lower rise times compared to MRAC operating with the same learning rate. Furthermore, FLMRAC also shows robust behaviour in situations such as partial thruster failure.

Author Keywords: Frequency Limited Model Reference Adaptive Control (FLMRAC)

articleTitle: Enhancing the Efficiency of a CdS/CdTe Solar Cell Cost Effectively with a BSF Layer
abstract: Second-generation solar cells, particularly Cadmium Telluride (CdTe) as a semiconductor material, represent a significant advancement in the photovoltaic industry. However, the combination of cost-effectiveness and high efficiency in CdTe solar cells has not been fully achieved, leaving a significant research gap. Starting from a laboratory-developed Cadmium Sulfide/Cadmium Telluride (CdS/CdTe) solar cell, this study performs a numerical study to obtain a methodology to enhance the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of that solar cell cost-effectively. Therefore, a novel mathematical model is developed to calculate the most optimum thickness for the CdTe layer to enhance the PCE of the cell cost-effectively. Subsequently, various materials for the Back Surface Field (BSF) layer are considered to optimize the electron-hole pair separation and reduce recombination losses while improving the PCE. Accordingly, Zinc Telluride (ZnTe) is the most appropriate material for the BSF layer. Finally, using optimum absorber layer thickness and selected BSF layer, the PCE of the CdS/CdTe solar cell is enhanced from $14.7 \%$ to $\mathbf{25.1\%}$.

articleTitle: Approach with Fuzzy Data Sets in Utility-Connected Solar Energy Systems for MPPT
abstract: In this paper, the application of the fuzzy logic approach in peak power tracking for utility-connected solar energy systems is unveiled. The fundamental aim of this paper is to employ the fuzzy-based approach efficiently for peak power tracking, enabling accurate monitoring of the maximum power in a photovoltaic system. This utility-connected solar energy system comprises solar panels, a DC/DC boost converter (for boosting the voltage levels of PV panels), a fuzzy-based power tracking controller, an inverter (for converting DC power into AC power), and the utility grid. This system employs two separate controllers: a fuzzy-based controller for precise tracking of PV power and a Synchronous reference frame phase locked loop controller for synchronizing the utility grid with the inverter to prevent any operational issues. The focus here is on optimizing the peak power tracking controller to fully utilize the potential of solar energy. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated by comparing it with traditional peak power tracking algorithms. The simulation studies are performed in MATLAB Simulink(2023b) software, with a 100 kilo-watt power level at a nominal grid frequency. The results are presented at the end to demonstrate that the fuzzy-based method reduces oscillations during power point tracking and exhibits a faster response compared to traditional hill climbing techniques, particularly in scenarios with swiftly changing operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable and Dual Functional On-Board Battery Charger For Electric Vehicles
abstract: The proposed work is an on-board electric vehicle charger featuring an interleaved totem-pole power factor correction (ITPFC) converter and a high-power isolated (HPI) DC-DC converter. The proposed charger operates in two modes, namely grid-connected mode (GCM) and driving mode (DM). In GCM, the ITPFC converter, together with the DC-DC converter, will charge the main battery. In DM, the ITPFC converter is reconfigured to an interleaved buck converter to charge the auxiliary battery of the electric vehicle from the main battery. This eliminates the need for an extra isolated DC-DC converter in the traditional chargers to charge the auxiliary loads, and the proposed charger configuration has fewer components. Thus, the on-board charger is cost effective with minimal consumption of the vehicles’ internal space. The charger offers isolation for the main battery in GCM and to the auxiliary battery in DM. Also, the back-end DC-DC converter has a soft-switching capability that improves the output power density and enhances the overall efficiency of the charger. The proposed on-board charger is designed for 7.2kW. This paper demonstrates the operation of charger in GCM and DM accompanied by the MATLAB results.

Author Keywords: Interleaved Totem-Pole Power Factor Correction Converter

articleTitle: An Economic Analysis of Optimized HESS with Pumped Hydro for Maximizing Solar Energy in Sri Lanka
abstract: The future world trend is towards decarbonization, considering that this research focuses on increasing renewable energy generation while minimizing thermal energy generation in power systems. When maximizing solar energy generation, energy storage can be used as a controllable resource to minimize solar energy curtailments. A Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) combines Pumped Hydro Storage (PHS) and Battery Storage (BS) to maximize the overall performance. Here, a techno-economic multi-objective optimization algorithm is introduced to size and cost solar PV and BS, while considering the optimal time to integrating PHS into the system. The proposed algorithm aims to minimize the total investment cost, the operation and maintenance cost, and the penalty cost incurred due to solar surplus and thermal (oil) generation. The genetic algorithm is used to achieve multi-objective optimization, implemented using the Pymoo open-source framework in Python. An energy management system is utilized to operating hours, ensuring proper regulation. Results are presented in a Pareto optimal chart for better analysis, and economic analyses were conducted for various PHS installation times. Finally, the optimal duration for integrating PHS, considering both economical and environment facts, was determined, with solar and BS capacities for each two-year interval throughout the planning horizon.

articleTitle: A 78.3% Efficient Power Management System Using FOCV-Based MPPT for Thermoelectric-Powered IoT Applications
abstract: This paper presents an efficient power management system (PMS) that uses thermoelectric energy generators (TEGs) as the power source for internet of things (IoT) applications. The PMS consists of a dynamically configured controller circuit ($\mathrm{DC}^{3}$), a startup circuit (SC), and a maximum power point (MPPT) controller. The DC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> utilizes six TEGs and a controller circuit to optimize the power from the TEGs, whether configured in series or parallel. The SC uses a transformer-based RLC oscillator and can start the overall system at the source voltage $V_{S}$ of 350 mV. The MPPT controller is based on a fractional open circuit voltage (FOCV) technique, and test results demonstrate that the tracking efficiency ($\eta_{\text {MPPT }}$) exceeds $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ for $V_{S}=\mathbf{1 0 0} \mathbf{~ m V}$. The PMS achieves a conversion efficiency ($\eta_{\text {Conv. }}$) of $\mathbf{7 8 . 3 \%}$ for $V_{S}=100 \mathrm{mV}$, indicating the successful operation of the proposed PMS.

articleTitle: An Optimized Speed Controller Design for IPMSM based-on Field-Oriented Control
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a speed-controlled Interior-Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) drive using an incremental position encoder. The control scheme is based on Field-Oriented Control (FOC), with the speed regulator modeled using the Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) technique utilizing the machine’s reluctance torque. A Vector-Tracking Observer (VTO) is designed for precise speed estimation based on rotor position. The dynamic performance of the drive is analyzed through experimental testing.

articleTitle: Energy Management System for Solar PV System to Reduce Peak Demand
abstract: Increasing rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems need efficient energy management strategies to improve the use of energy and reduce costs. This paper presents an energy management system (EMS) for grid-connected solar PV and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to reduce the burden on the grid during peak demand periods by supplying power from BESS that is charged by the generated solar power to the load and improving power flow within the system to achieve cost-effective energy usage. This approach reduces dependence on the grid at peak demand times and reduces power consumption costs. EMS manages BESS charging and discharging processes and power flow among the load, grid, and BESS while supplying reactive power to the load. A simulation interface is used to model the system consisting of the PV system, BESS, and load. The proposed EMS is developed and verified using the simulation. The results are compared to the performance of the PV system with and without the proposed EMS, which illustrates the performance of EMS in improving power sharing and reducing energy costs.

articleTitle: Intelligent Beach Cleaning Robot with Dual Modes of Refuse Collection and YOLO-based Detection
abstract: Coastal pollution, driven by the accumulation of plastics and debris on beaches, poses a serious threat to natural habitats and marine ecosystems. Manual cleaning efforts, while valiant, are labor intensive and insufficient to address the scale of the problem. Intelligent beach cleaning robots offer a promising solution by integrating advanced technology with environmental stewardship. This paper reviews existing robotic refuse collection mechanisms and introduces an Intelligent Beach Cleaning Robot equipped with dual modes of refuse collection mechanisms (raking and sieving shaker), object detection, autonomous navigation, and obstacle avoidance systems. Through rigorous testing and analysis, we achieved an accuracy of $93 \%$ in plastic debris detection using the YOLOv5 model. The robot’s raking mechanism effectively collects debris within a 6 -second time frame, while the sieving shaker mechanism operates at an optimal frequency of 2.5 Hz for efficient sand filtration. The proposed prototype aims to improve the refuse collection capabilities cost-effectively, addressing the critical need for adaptable and efficient beach cleaning solutions.

articleTitle: Enhanced PMSM Current Controller via DOB-Based Load Torque Forecasting
abstract: The current control of the D and Q axes of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) is crucial in drives, especially when saliency is present in the system. The stability and performance of any outer loop control algorithm are significantly influenced by the performance of the D and Q axis current controllers. The outer loop typically functions as a speed or torque controller, often incorporating an MTPA. This paper proposes an inner loop controller that observes changes in load torque and adjusts the current components accordingly. To determine the load torque in the proposed model, a disturbance observer (DOB) approach is utilized, which eliminates the need for external load torque sensors. Unlike usual DOB approaches, this method considers disturbance torque for both Iq and Id inner loops. The predicted torque is calculated based on the references of D and Q axis currents, and the difference between dynamic torques is used to forecast the load torque. The forecasted load torque is then used to calculate the dq axis currents, which are injected back into the system. The PMSM and drive system were simulated under various torque inputs, comparing results for scenarios with and without the proposed controller, while keeping all other parameters constant. As the results are derived from a simulation environment, validating the proposed method through hardware implementation and analyzing the variations will be a critical aspect of future research. Simulation results demonstrate that the current controller incorporating the proposed method exhibits improved performance compared to the scenario without the proposed controller.

articleTitle: A Correlation Between Eccentricity Fault and AC Winding Losses of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
abstract: In this study, the variation of AC winding losses in a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) under eccentricity fault conditions is investigated. To analyze how AC winding losses change during eccentricity faults, the motor is simulated using ANSYS@Motor-CAD software under static, dynamic, and mixed (static + dynamic) eccentricity faults. Analyses are conducted with three different stator conductor types and at various operating frequencies. The obtained results are extensively analyzed and compared for both healthy and eccentric motors. The analysis results show that the AC winding losses in the faulty condition increase compared to the healthy condition.

articleTitle: Technical Impacts of High Penetration of Solar Photovoltaic Systems in Low-Voltage Radial Distribution Network – Case Study
abstract: Rapid integration of Solar Photovoltaic (PV) based Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) at the distribution network has posed challenges to the grid operators since higher solar PV penetration coincides with the lower load demand, leading to issues like reverse power flow, overvoltage, harmonic current injection in the low-voltage (LV) network. In this paper, a realistic LV electric distribution network in the Kalmunai area, which is operated by the main utility provider in Sri Lanka, is modeled in ETAP software. The impact of PV penetration on transformer’s loading, power factor, power flow, power losses, and voltage profile of LV feeders are plotted and analyzed. Furthermore, the analysis is extended by considering various irradiance levels for different PV penetrations. Subsequently, the variation of voltage profile for solar PV concentrated feeder is plotted under various irradiance levels for different PV penetrations. The results indicate that overvoltage condition occurs at concentrated solar PV feeder, when the irradiance is high $\left(900 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}\right.$ and above), and the PV penetration is after the zero-crossing point. Additionally, the results show that reverse power flow occurs through the transformer when the aggregated solar PV active power generation exceeds the total active power demand of customers within the LV distribution network, which typically occurs during mid-day time (lower load demand time) when irradiance is higher ($\mathbf{9 0 0} \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ and above).

articleTitle: Comparison of Appliance Signature Classification Methods for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a vital technique for disaggregating individual appliance loads from aggregated household energy consumption data. In this study, we utilize the PLAID dataset to conduct a comprehensive review of various classification methods employed in NILM systems. We focus on traditional machine learning approaches such as support vector machines (SVM), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and random forests (RF), as well as modern deep learning models like multi-layer perceptrons (MLP) and convolutional neural networks (CNN). Our analysis examines the effect of different sampling frequencies on the performance of these models, highlighting the strengths and limitations of each under varying conditions. The insights provided in this paper offer valuable guidance for researchers and practitioners in selecting the most effective classification techniques for their specific NILM applications.

articleTitle: Development of a Dynamic Stability and Obstacle Navigation Optimization Mechanism in Mobile Robots via Active Suspension and PID Control
abstract: The field of robotics marks a significant turning point in contemporary technology. New designs and solutions are developed every day in this robotics industry, and their benefits are enormous. Mobile robots are thought to be one of the most remarkable inventions among them. Many mobile robots have built-in obstacle recognition and avoidance capabilities. However, not much focus has been placed on creating mobile robots that can identify and avoid obstacles. This study introduces an innovative way to address this gap. The goal of this project is to design and create an active suspension framework for a mobile robot, which will enable the robot to advance, get past obstacles, and become more stable and mobile. The robot’s active suspension mechanism is assessed theoretically and experimentally utilizing various sloped surfaces. This robot is remarkable in that it constantly tries to maintain horizontal and avoid bending and rolling. Furthermore, implementing this innovative technique can solve important problems, including the intricacy of the current robot suspension system’s design, the complexity of the control systems, and the increase in production prices.

articleTitle: Economical Sizing of an Energy Storage System for a Community Microgrid, through the Designing of a Smart Demand Response Technology
abstract: Formation of “duck curve” is becoming a concerning topic in the power industry. This causes the power systems to dispatch expensive power generation during peak hours, and creates a burden to the utility in power system planning and operation. Although community microgrid is an effective solution, the cost of deployment becomes a barrier. The costliest component of the microgrid is the energy storage. To overcome this problem, a smart demand response technology is introduced at the planning stage to size the battery economically. Smart demand response technology consists of two parts, as forecasting model to predict the demand curve and real time pricing model to guide the consumers to follow the expected demand curve. Expected demand curve is obtained through peak clipping of the predicted demand curve by a predetermined percentage. Real time pricing is implemented based on the expected demand curve, which allowed to reduce the battery size.

articleTitle: Brain-Controlled Wheelchair Navigation Using Visual Perception in Simulated Indoor Environments
abstract: Wheelchair navigation based on the Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) has gained significant attention due to its ease of use and offering support to people with severe paralysis in mobility. Enhancing the comfort of such people to use wheelchairs with more efficiency is essential to make it a practical application. In this research endeavor, a novel system based on Steady State Visually Evoked Potential (SSVEP) is introduced to autonomously guide a wheelchair from its initial location to a predetermined destination point. In this research, four distinct flickering frequencies serve as visual stimuli to represent specific locations within a simulated indoor environment. Electroencephalography (EEG) signals are acquired using a set of six electrodes, and signal preprocessing involves Common Average Referencing (CAR). To classify the EEG signals, a novel approach combines Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Power Spectrum Density (PSD) analyses, along with peak detection and thresholding techniques. The experiments were conducted in real-time, involving five subjects, each participating in six trials for every distinct frequency. Remarkably, the algorithm achieved an accuracy rate exceeding 90% for each frequency without prior training. Navigation based on the classified SSVEP frequencies was successfully executed within a simulation environment, using the Robot Operating System (ROS2), resulting in favorable outcomes. This promising result suggests the potential for future implementations through the integration of appropriate hardware and sensors.

articleTitle: Electricity Demand Response to Price Changes in Sri Lanka
abstract: This study investigates the responsiveness of electricity consumers to the price changes in Sri Lanka, by means of estimating the short-term price elasticity of demand. The electricity consumption data for a period of 6 months, from a selected consumer sample, across a tariff increase event is considered. The findings of the study are categorized based on the consumer groups, namely ‘Household’, ‘Commercial’ and ‘Industrial’. The direct price elasticity is observed to be highest for the ‘Industrial’ consumer group, compared to the others. In addition to the above, the peak to non-peak substitution with price is also studied for ‘Industrial’ and ‘Commercial’ consumer groups. It shows that the ‘Industrial’ consumers are more responsive to peak, non-peak price variations, in comparison to ‘Commercial’ consumers.

articleTitle: Correction of Ships’ Steering Angle for Safe Maneuvering Against Strong Winds Using Microcontroller
abstract: The maritime industry, which handles approximately 80% of global trade volume, faces significant challenges from adverse weather conditions, particularly strong winds. Over-steering with the strong wind condition will increase the risk of capsizing, leading to substantial economic and human losses. This paper develops a microcontroller-based system to correct ships’ steering angles in real-time based on wind conditions, thereby enhancing navigational safety. The system utilizes wind speed and direction transducers, gyro modules, and GPS receivers to continuously monitor environmental conditions and navigational parameters. The data are processed by a microcontroller using a developed mathematical model which assess wind impact on the ship’s motion and calculates necessary adjustments to the steering angle to counteract wind forces, ensuring stable and safe manoeuvring. Key factors in the model include wind force, circular motion force, and heel angle, providing a comprehensive assessment of ship stability under varying wind conditions. The system is designed to work with existing steering mechanisms, ensuring cost-effectiveness and ease of implementation. Simulations demonstrate the system ability to predict and correct steering angles accurately, reducing the risk of over-steering and capsizing. Rigorous testing validates the system performance, showing significant improvements in navigational safety under strong wind conditions. The proposed solution offers a robust method to enhance maritime safety, protecting both crew and cargo.

articleTitle: User evaluation of cylindrical electrostatic clutch based haptic force feedback glove in teleoperation system
abstract: Motivated by the potential of robotic teleoperation systems to augment the capabilities of both human operators and controlled robots, we have developed a wearable haptic force feedback glove that enables operators to control the index finger of a 3D-printed robot hand. Conventional force feedback haptic gloves predominantly utilize rigid actuators such as electric motors and pneumatic cylinders, which are encumbered by safety concerns, weightiness, and intricate transmission mechanisms. To overcome these challenges, our research focuses on evaluating a lightweight, cost-effective feedback glove utilizing an electrostatic clutch and a flexible rack and pinion gear finger tracking mechanism. Evaluation through participant experiments indicates a positive reception of the haptic force feedback glove, with users generally expressing satisfaction regarding its weight, comfort, ease of use, and overall performance. Importantly, we evaluated these three areas considering gender as an individual factor. However, further refinement of the haptic feedback system may be necessary to enhance user experience and address any concerns raised by participants. Moreover, the proposed glove could hold potential for application in virtual reality grasping scenarios, providing users with realistic haptic feedback experiences.

articleTitle: Development of a Model to Determine Optimum Unit Capacities and Number of Turbines for a Given Mini-hydro Site and Flow Regime
abstract: Mini-hydropower plants offer a promising renewable energy solution for developing countries due to their relatively low investment costs and ability to provide reliable electricity to remote communities. Nevertheless, fine-tuning the layout of these plants with a view to obtaining maximum energy yield at the lowest possible costs is a big challenge. This paper presents a new mathematical model that can be used to determine the optimal unit capacities and number of turbines for a particular mini-hydro site and for a given flow regime. By considering key factors such as available water head, flow regime, equipment efficiencies, expected lifetime and economic parameters such as inflation and discount rate, model gives the most optimum turbine configuration. Graphical user interface (GUI) has been developed to ensure ease of use. Advantages provided by this model include efficiency, optimality, cost effectiveness, ease of use and adaptability, empower decision makers to maximize their benefits by identifying the most cost-effective solution for their mini hydro project. This work contributes to the development of cost-effective renewable energy solutions, thus advancing the transition towards a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Online Partial Discharge Detection & Localization of a Transformer Winding Using Machine Learning
abstract: Power transformers are critical and costly components in power systems. The primary cause of severe failures in power transformers is insulation breakdown and partial discharge (PD) is a significant contributor to insulation failure due to gradual erosion. Therefore, accurate detection and localization of PD are essential for effective condition monitoring. This research introduces a robust approach for detecting and pinpointing PD using machine learning, eliminating the need for human intervention and dismantling the transformer, thereby enhancing the reliability of power systems. Using a lumped parameter RLC model in PSCAD, PD is simulated by injecting current impulses at various winding locations. Terminal current waveforms are analyzed to extract features for machine learning training. The study also focuses on identifying multiple winding locations of the transformer in cases where partial discharge might be found in multiple locations. The study indicates that statistical features are most effective in accurately representing PD, with Support Vector Machine exhibiting higher accuracy compared to other machine learning methods for partial discharge monitoring.

articleTitle: Emotion-Responsive and Interactive Self-reconfigurable Robot for Children
abstract: The use of interactive robots in early education, harnessing their fascinating potential to enhance children’s play and learning experiences, is well-documented in the literature. Reconfigurable robots, on the other hand, have demonstrated their advantages over fixed-shaped robots in various domains. However, they have not yet been utilized as interactive companions for children. Integrating reconfiguration into interactive learning and playing robots adds a new dimension to their versatility and adaptability. This paper explores the use of a reconfigurable robot as an interactive playing and learning platform for children. In this context, a vision-based method was developed to perceive a child’s emotional state and head pose. Fuzzy logic was employed to determine the robot’s behavior based on the child’s emotional state and head pose variations. The robot’s movement speed, direction, configuration, and color were adjusted to interact with the user. The experimental results validate that the proposed method enables a reconfigurable robot to interact with a user based on variations in emotional levels.

articleTitle: Improved Maximum Power Point Tracking of Standalone Solar PV system for Faster and Accurate Convergence
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays exhibit a nonlinear relationship between power (P) and voltage (V) when exposed to consistent solar irradiation, typically resulting in a single maximum power point (MPP) on the Power - Voltage curve within the operational voltage range. However, varying weather conditions can lead to the appearance of multiple MPPs, complicating the task of pinpointing the optimal operating voltage for achieving absolute maximum power. To address this challenge, this research proposes an enhanced maximum power point tracking (MPPT) method that incorporates fuzzy logic. The aim is to achieve expedited and more precise convergence to the MPP, irrespective of stable or varying weather conditions. The results show that the improved tracking algorithm decreases the time to reach the MPP by 47% compared to traditional hill climbing algorithms. The study uses MATLAB/Simulink to mathematically model a photovoltaic array. The proposed method is simulated and compared with various commercially available MPPT techniques, including traditional hill-climbing methods. It uses simulated and empirical results to validate the enhanced efficacy of the method. Additionally, the paper discusses the development of an economical solar charge controller incorporating the advanced MPPT algorithm, emphasizing practical applications and improvements in real-world efficiency.

articleTitle: Intelligent Sinhala Question and Answer System by Incorporating Visual Clues
abstract: This research aims to develop an intelligent Sinhala question-and-answer system to enhance technological resources for Sinhala language processing. This AI-driven system will provide an interactive platform for college students to engage in conversational, object-based learning in Sinhala. Voice input will facilitate questions, and responses will be delivered in Sinhala audio, enhancing immersion and usability. This manages a local Mongo database for knowledge storage and retrieval of the data system that wants access to relevant information. This interactive Sinhala Q&A system used BERT model achitecute and it is trained on Sinhala dataset. Overall system has capability to adapt according to objects available in the vision field and then generate responses based on the object specific context. Object identification is done by YOLO model. In addition to developing a Sinhala BERT NLP model, Sinhala NLP Wordpiece tokenizer and Sinhala Dataset suitable for Sinhala BERT model are developed. Following result of this research can show that this system is an effective tool. When showing Banana to the system and asking ? (What are bananas?), system voice output will be (a fruit). In conclusion, this research will contribute to the field of educational technology and by developing this system, college students will have access to a tool that can assist them in improving their knowledge and proficiency in the Sinhala language.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based Solar Power Nowcasting with Real-time Cloud Path Prediction
abstract: The integration of solar power into Sri Lanka’s power grid is challenged by the intermittent nature of solar energy due to cloud cover. This research presents an intelligent control system for real-time cloud path prediction and solar power forecasting. Utilizing a sky-imaging device with a fisheye lens and CMOS IMX179 sensor, the system captures high-resolution sky images. A custom YOLOv8 model detects clouds and the sun, while ByteTrack and centroid-based tracking analyze cloud trajectories. Reinforcement learning is employed to predict cloud trajectories, and a random forest algorithm forecasts power output fluctuations. Results demonstrate the system’s effectiveness in providing accurate, real-time solar power forecasts, contributing to enhanced grid stability and supporting renewable energy goals in Sri Lanka.

articleTitle: Intelligent Battery Management Algorithm for Second-Life Battery Systems Using Voltage Based Active Cell Balancing
abstract: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are widely used in the present for domestic and commercial applications. Energy generated from renewable and non-renewable sources will be stored in BESS for utilization on demand. Lithium-ion battery cells are mostly used in present BESS due to the main advantages of high energy density and longer cycle life. Lithium-ion battery cells need strict control of cell voltage and cell temperature within operating ranges using Battery Management System (BMS) for safety and longevity. With the rapidly growing Electric Vehicle (EV) usage in the world, Lithium-ion battery cells used in EVs are used for BESS for second-life usage. Unlike first-life battery cells, Second-Life Battery (SLB) cells tend to develop cell capacity mismatches due to cycle life and non-homogenous temperature variations during first-life usage. The cell capacity mismatch causes cell voltage imbalance which leads to usable capacity reduction and accelerated degradation. The traditional passive BMSs are not sufficient to overcome cell capacity mismatch in SLB cells. This paper presents Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) based relative cell capacity estimation with Reinforced Learning (RL) based active cell balancing algorithm. A simulated virtual model of a SLB system is used for the analysis which replicates the actual battery cell parameters. The performance of the introduced algorithm is evaluated in comparison with a conventional passive BMS algorithm. Compared with the conventional approaches, the proposed method eliminates the exposure of the low-capacity cells to extended highest and lowest cell voltage conditions improving the overall performance of SLB systems.
